boards.title: Your First Weekend at Stanford University, Shared as Cards
boards.description: A low-key, under-21-safe first-weekend sequence of campus landmarks, art, gardens, and a daytime trail.

cards.title: Begin with a campus orientation
cards.subtitle: 295 Galvez Street · Friday daytime
cards.notes: Pick up current visitor information, then use the campus map or a self-guided route to choose landmarks that fit your available time.
cards.short_summary: A practical starting point for getting situated on campus.
cards.evidence_claim: Stanford states that its Visitor Center provides campus-visit information and is generally open weekdays from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m., subject to holidays and breaks.
cards.access_notes: Generally weekdays 9 a.m.–5 p.m.; confirm exceptions before going.

cards.title: Walk through the Main Quad
cards.subtitle: Central campus · Friday afternoon
cards.notes: Enter through Memorial Court from Palm Drive and take a slow lap through Stanford’s original classroom buildings before moving toward the arts district.
cards.short_summary: A central-campus walk anchored by Stanford’s historic core.
cards.evidence_claim: Stanford identifies the Main Quad as holding its 12 original classrooms and Memorial Court as its main entrance from Palm Drive.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor landmark; follow posted campus guidance.

cards.title: Pause at Memorial Church
cards.subtitle: Main Quad · Friday afternoon
cards.notes: Make this a short architecture stop: view the exterior and use Stanford’s visitor materials to plan any interior visit around the church’s access guidance.
cards.short_summary: A historic landmark at the heart of the Quad.
cards.evidence_claim: Stanford’s visitor guide lists Memorial Church among campus destinations and directs visitors to its history and visit information.
cards.access_notes: Check the church’s own visitor guidance before expecting interior access.

cards.title: Spend an afternoon with art
cards.subtitle: 328 Lomita Drive · Friday or weekend
cards.notes: Choose a few galleries rather than rushing the whole museum, and check the visitor guidelines for the day’s opening time and gallery rules.
cards.short_summary: A free museum stop with galleries and visitor amenities.
cards.evidence_claim: Cantor Arts Center says admission is always free and lists public hours Wednesday through Sunday, including later Thursday hours.
cards.source_title: Our Visitor Guidelines | Cantor Arts Center
cards.access_notes: No advance reservation required; verify hours and gallery rules before arrival.

cards.title: Continue next door at the Anderson
cards.subtitle: 314 Lomita Drive · Friday or weekend
cards.notes: Use the adjacent museum as a second, focused art stop; look for the listed open days first, since it is closed Tuesdays and Wednesdays.
cards.short_summary: Modern and contemporary American art in Stanford’s arts district.
cards.evidence_claim: The Anderson Collection describes itself as a free museum of modern and contemporary American art and lists Thursday–Monday hours of 11 a.m.–5 p.m.
cards.source_title: Visit | Anderson Collection at Stanford University
cards.access_notes: Open Thursday–Monday, 11 a.m.–5 p.m.; closed Tuesday and Wednesday.

cards.title: Find the sculpture garden
cards.subtitle: Campus garden · Saturday morning
cards.notes: Walk the garden slowly and read the interpretive information on-site; the carvings reward a closer look more than a quick pass-through.
cards.short_summary: An outdoor garden of wood and stone carvings.
cards.evidence_claim: Stanford says the garden contains 40 wood and stone carvings created on-site in 1994 by ten artists from the inland Sepik River area.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor destination; use the campus map for its current route and access.

cards.title: Take a garden detour
cards.subtitle: Near central campus · Saturday midday
cards.notes: Bring water and make this a daylight walk; follow paths through the garden and leave plants, structures, and wildlife undisturbed.
cards.short_summary: A historic garden designed for Jane and Leland Stanford.
cards.evidence_claim: Stanford states that landscape architect Rudolf Ulrich designed the Arizona Cactus Garden for Jane and Leland Stanford between 1881 and 1883.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor destination; visit during daylight and follow posted rules.

cards.title: Circle Lake Lagunita
cards.subtitle: Campus west side · Saturday afternoon
cards.notes: Use the lake as a quiet walking break, keeping to appropriate paths and treating it as a view-and-stroll stop whether the basin is wet or dry.
cards.short_summary: A campus lake area for a daytime walk and view.
cards.evidence_claim: Stanford identifies Lake Lagunita as a place to run, walk, or enjoy the view, noting that it may be dry.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor destination; respect any posted access restrictions.

cards.title: Save the Dish for a daylight hike
cards.subtitle: 400 Reservoir Road · Sunday daytime
cards.notes: Plan a daylight loop with water and shoes for uneven ground, stay on designated recreational routes, and check the status page before leaving.
cards.short_summary: A 3.5-mile campus foothill trail with seasonal access hours.
cards.evidence_claim: Stanford describes the Dish as a 3.5-mile trail and publishes seasonal public-access hours; its current site says April–August access is 6 a.m.–7:30 p.m.
cards.access_notes: Access hours vary by season and the area can close for maintenance or fire conditions; check the status page before visiting.

cards.entity_name: Green East After Hours Study Area
cards.title: End with a late-night study reset
cards.subtitle: Hohbach Hall, Green Library · Sunday night
cards.notes: If you have Stanford ID access and classes are in session, settle in with one small task for Monday and leave time to get proper rest.
cards.short_summary: An overnight study area for Stanford ID holders during the academic term.
cards.evidence_claim: Stanford Libraries says Green East’s after-hours study area is open midnight–8 a.m. Sunday through Thursday when classes are in session.
cards.source_title: Green East After Hours Study Area | Stanford University Libraries
cards.access_notes: Open midnight–8 a.m. Sunday–Thursday when classes are in session; access is for Stanford ID holders and holiday closures occur.
